title: Edge DNS & Egress Patterns for Private Deployments (workshop notes)
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and option comparisons from the 2025-11-03 internal workshop for customer POCs that require private networking (VPC-to-VPC + on-prem/VPC egress) for Redwood Private deployments. Goal: give SEs a usable cheat-sheet for recommended patterns (peering vs TGW vs PrivateLink), DNS approaches (split-horizon, resolver endpoints), and egress control patterns for regulated customers.

Audience
---
Solutions engineers, infra architects, and customer cloud/network engineers running private POCs or preparing deployment proposals.

Key constraints observed in customer POCs
---
- Multi-account setups (customer has separate accounts for dev/stage/prod)
- Need to avoid public subnets for inference nodes in regulated customers
- Requirement for egress control and logging (allow-listing external services, central proxy)
- Low-latency path to customer internal services (auth, config, model stores)
- DNS visibility across accounts and to on-prem (service discovery)

Design patterns (short summary)
---
1) Small-scale (<5 accounts), low complexity: VPC Peering + Route 53 private hosted zones
   - Pros: low operational overhead, simpler routing, cheaper than TGW at small scale
   - Cons: N^2 peering scale problem, manual route table updates across accounts

2) Medium/large-scale (>5 accounts) or multi-region: Transit Gateway (TGW)
   - Pros: scalable, central routing, supports central egress/inspection VPCs, easier cross-account attachments via RAM
   - Cons: cost, introduces single routing plane; need TGW route propagation discipline

3) Service isolation + vendor-hosted integrations: PrivateLink (Interface endpoints) and NLB fronting
   - Pros: fine-grained service-level access without exposing subnets, strong access control via SGs and resource policies
   - Cons: per-service cost, extra management for endpoint lifecycle

4) On-prem hybrid: Route 53 Resolver + AWS Outbound/Inboud Endpoints or DNS forwarders in customer network
   - Use resolver inbound endpoints to allow on-prem to resolve private hosted zones; outbound endpoints to let VPCs resolve on-prem names.

DNS approaches (detailed)
---
- Route 53 private hosted zones attached to the account VPC(s) for internal discovery. For cross-account lookup: share the private hosted zone via Resource Access Manager (RAM) or replicate zones per-account (tradeoffs below).
- Split-horizon DNS: keep public records in public hosted zone; private records in private hosted zone. For customers with hybrid DNS needs, use Route 53 Resolver rules to forward specific domains to on-prem DNS servers.
- If customer uses GCP/Azure on-prem DNS, plan for cross-cloud forwarding (resolver endpoints + endpoints in TGW/CNIs).

Egress control patterns
---
1) Central Egress VPC (recommended for regulated POCs)
   - All outbound traffic from inference VPCs is routed to a central egress VPC via TGW or peering. The egress VPC contains an inspection stack: NAT Gateway / proxy (squid/nginx) / IDS / logging.
   - Benefits: centralized logging, single IP allow-listing for external partners, easier proxy configuration for token/key exfiltration prevention.

2) Per-VPC NAT + Egress proxy
   - Simpler but proliferates public IPs and makes external partner allow-listing harder. Not preferred if partner requires single egress IP(s).

3) PrivateConnect / Direct Connect / VPN + customer FW
   - For on-prem-bound egress or contracts requiring direct circuits. Combine with route filters and BGP community tagging for route control.

Common security controls to apply
---
- Security group least-privilege: inference nodes should only allow inbound from trusted management and model-store CIDRs and ephemeral SSH from bastion (if needed).
- NACLs for subnet-level inbound/outbound hardening where customer policy requires defense-in-depth.
- IAM roles for cross-account access to S3/model artifacts; use STS assume-role with tight conditions.
- VPC Flow Logs (centralized) and Mirror sessions for detailed packet capture if requested.

Sample route / SG snippets (copy-paste friendly)
---
- Route table entry to TGW: 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-abc123 (central-egress)
- Security group (inference nodes): allow outbound 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 only if routed via central egress; otherwise restrict to proxy IPs
- Example SG rule text: "Allow outbound HTTPS to egress-proxy.example.internal (10.10.5.12/32)"

CIDR planning guidances
---
- Reserve /16 per environment if you expect many subnets; example: prod 10.20.0.0/16, stage 10.21.0.0/16, dev 10.22.0.0/16.
- Avoid overlapping with customer on-prem ranges; confirm with customer netops and put in the proposal.

Decision matrix (short)
---
- Required single-source egress IP for 3rd party allow-listing: Central Egress VPC + TGW or Direct Connect
- Customer forbids Internet egress from inference hosts: Use PrivateLink for model updates and S3 Gateway endpoints + pull updates via VPC endpoints only; push metrics to on-prem via secured VPN
- Need sub-100ms latency to on-prem services: prioritize Direct Connect or colocated peering; test in a short spike POC before committing

Workshop recap / actions taken 2025-11-03
---
- Decided on 2 starter templates for SEs to use during demos:
  1) "Small peered POC": single-account customer, VPC peering to customer VPC, private hosted zone shared via RAM, per-VPC NAT disabled in favor of central NAT proxy in a shared tools account.
  2) "Scale-ready POC": TGW-based transit with egress vpc and resolver endpoints; recommended when customer expects >3 accounts or multi-region.
- Implemented skeleton CloudFormation/Terraform for template (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/networking-proposals/pull/58).
- Action: add quick test script to validate DNS resolution across accounts and TTL behavior (owner: Ethan Park, due: 2025-11-17).

Open questions (for next workshop with customer netops)
---
- Do they require TLS inspection at the proxy? If yes, we need to discuss cert management and potential privacy/regulatory implications.
- Do customer on-prem DNS servers permit forwarding from AWS resolver endpoints? Some enterprise DNS teams require a formal request.
- What is their allowed public CIDR ranges for egress IP allow-listing? Need the explicit list.

Suggested POC checklist (pre-flight)
---
- [ ] Confirm exact CIDR ranges for all accounts and on-prem
- [ ] Confirm DNS domains to be resolved across networks
- [ ] Decide peering vs TGW based on number of accounts and expected growth
- [ ] Confirm logging/retention requirements for VPC Flow Logs and egress logs
- [ ] Check partner allow-listing requirements and whether single egress IP needed
- [ ] Create IAM roles and least-privilege policies for cross-account S3/model artifact access

Appendix: quick ASCII diagram (typical TGW central egress pattern)
---
  +----------------------+       +-----------------+       +--------------+
  | Customer Account A   |-------|    TGW (core)   |-------| Egress VPC   |
  | 10.20.0.0/16 (VPC1)  |       | (attachments)   |       | 10.30.0.0/24 |
  +----------------------+       +--------+--------+       +------+-------+
                                               |                     |
                                               |                     |-> NAT GW / proxy -> Internet (single egress IP)
                                               |
                                   +-----------+-----------+
                                   | Customer Account B     |
                                   | 10.21.0.0/16 (VPC2)    |
                                   +------------------------+

Notes on replicability for SEs
---
- Keep the TF modules parameterized: allow toggling between TGW/Peering/PrivateLink, and toggle resolver endpoints.
- Provide smoke tests: (1) DNS resolution across accounts, (2) curl to external endpoint and verify source IP matches expected egress IP, (3) S3 access via gateway endpoint.

Next steps (owner assignments)
---
- Ethan Park: add DNS validation script and include in the TF modules (due 2025-11-17).
- Maya Singh: update SE playbook with decision matrix and sample email template for requesting on-prem DNS forwarding (due 2025-11-21).
- Sofia Martinez: prepare condensed one-pager for customer-facing proposal that summarizes options and cost tradeoffs (due 2025-11-13).

If you're using this doc in a pre-sales call: start with the customer's scale goals (accounts, regions), list their egress policy constraints, and then present 2 options (simple peering vs TGW central-egress) with an estimated cost delta.

End of notes.
